result_text:
The per-extension entries are now named by the bare lower-cased extension (`"java"`, `"js"`, `"html"`), and the landscape aggregation merges old and new spellings. The two codeanalyzer test classes I updated pass (`NamedSourceCodeAspectTest`, `CodeConfigurationTest`). I did not add a test for the landscape merge.

**Changes, all in `codeanalyzer`:**
- `aspects/SourceCodeAspectUtils.java`: `getAspectsPerExtensions` creates entries named `extension` instead of `"  *." + extension`. This also changes the names from `getScopesWithExtensions()`.
- `analysis/AnalysisUtils.java`: the metric ids drop the `replace("*.", "")` since names are already bare. The ids come out the same (`MAIN_EXT_JAVA`). The textual summary line still prints `  *.java: …` because I prepend `"  *."` there.
- `landscape/analysis/LandscapeAnalysisResults.java`: a new `getBareExtension` helper (strips a leading `*.`, trims, lower-cases) is used in the per-repository loop and in `merge()` for the build/generated/other category. Old `"  *.java"` and new `"java"` now collapse into one entry, and each contributing repository is still added to its description.
- `CodeConfigurationTest.java` and `NamedSourceCodeAspectTest.java`: the assertions now expect the bare names.

I left the `replace("*.", "")` calls in the `reports` module alone. Per-repository landscape pages read raw JSON from repositories analyzed before the change, so those calls still matter there. I did not run `mvn install`, so `reports` runs against the previously installed `codeanalyzer` jar. Nothing is committed.
